program: Finite counseling health within school resilience and educator support

nutshell.headline: Sustained counseling is real, but the measured clinical component is small relative to whole spending
nutshell.body: The research list uses the central scenario: $340,080,357 per 10 Bay QALYs. Signed mixture $188,291,084 per 10 Bay QALYs; central $340,080,357. This is full expense divided by partial quantified counseling health, not complete expected value.
nutshell.whyItMayWork: On-site relationship-based therapy can help underserved youth who otherwise lack suitable sustained care.
nutshell.whyWeAreCautious: The annual report identifies 24 clients and their families, not thousands of clinical courses. Educator support and SEL may matter, but their health effects are not quantified here.
nutshell.recommendationBlocker: HOLD giving recommendation. No verified priced marginal capacity, and even the favorable modeled clinical world is above $1M per 10 Bay QALYs.

programSection.body: The current annual report documents counseling, educator consultation/coaching, SEL and outreach in Peninsula/South Bay schools. Form 990 specifically describes relationship-based, trauma-informed Beechwood counseling. An undated services page describes a broader high-school footprint; it does not override the current reported clinical denominator.

steps.title: Count clinical clients, not reach
steps.detail: Use 24 index youth, with 484 total sessions including 31 family sessions. Do not add family members or multiply 11,000 indirect students by a clinical effect.

steps.title: Credit finite additional symptom health

steps.title: Keep whole-gift boundaries
steps.detail: Retain all $1,599,738 of expense, existing funded baseline and uncertain ordinary-cash response. Other health pathways remain unknown, not zero.

programSection.boundary: Counseling-only health numerator with whole-organization cost. No suicide survival awards from 23 interventions called life-saving by the organization. No teacher satisfaction-to-QALY conversion or training reach counted as completed care.

equation.label: Finite signed counseling component
equation.expression: gift / whole expense × cash response × Bay share × [24 index clients × completion × utility × duration × transfer × access increment − 24 × harm]

inputs.label: Whole annual expense
inputs.basis: Filed expense, including outreach, consultation, therapy, fundraising and administration. Not $167,455 Beechwood-only spending. External donated complements unpriced.

inputs.label: Index counseling clients
inputs.basis: Annual report p7: 24 clients and their families, 484 sessions and 19 average sessions/student. Count youth once, not family members or sessions; group/other pathways unquantified. These are not necessarily completed courses.

inputs.label: Meaningful course fraction
inputs.basis: Nineteen average sessions supports sustained engagement but is not a completion or outcome rate. Higher than unknown-throughput Rainbow; judgment.

inputs.label: Conditional average utility improvement
inputs.range: 0–.1 in base worlds; signed overrides allowed
inputs.basis: No local preference-based utility. Same .03/.06/.1 positive family as Rainbow. Conditional average for a meaningful completed course, not imported trial ITT.

inputs.label: Finite health duration
inputs.basis: Same positive horizon family as Rainbow. Persistence and time until an alternative can deliver comparable benefit; no lifetime mental-health credit.

inputs.label: Clinical population/modality transfer
inputs.basis: Younger elementary-age/complex-trauma and relationship-based care differs from depressed adolescent CBT trials. Lower central transfer than Rainbow .65 is judgment, not measured relative quality.

inputs.label: Counterfactual care increment
inputs.basis: Probability/fraction of modeled clinical improvement not obtained through school counselors, public services or other care. Separate from duration among incremental cases.

inputs.label: Ordinary-cash response
inputs.basis: Conditional cash-created delivery relative to historical whole budget; existing school contracts/grants retained. Does not claim deficit equals funding gap.

inputs.label: Bay health share
inputs.basis: San Mateo/Santa Clara service footprint; patient residences not observed. Applies equally to harms.

inputs.label: Burden per index client
inputs.basis: Independent short-lived adverse/burden allowance across all clients, including noncompleters; not a documented local harm rate.

inputs.label: Signed scenario weights
inputs.basis: Pre-output subjective beliefs, not calibrated probabilities.

model.uncertaintyBoundary: Favorable share 96.7645%. Subjective mass below $1M and $100k is zero in the declared worlds, not proof no such pathway exists. The partial numerator omits major educator and SEL work. Conditional utility-duration assumptions do not import an ITT effect and then penalize completion again. Annual report p7 is the current denominator; older 7,357/10,965 counseling hours refer to earlier periods and may have different service scope. No silent pooling. All-beneficiary price $188,166,837 is not the Bay price.
model.fundingBoundary: FY2025 IRS expense $1,599,738; revenue $1,467,064; program revenue $1,116,502 and government contributions $55,000. Prior expense $2,490,164. Net assets $163,416 include $108,416 without donor restrictions and $55,000 restricted; liabilities $88,774. Annual report revenue $1,525,397 includes released restrictions and differs from IRS revenue; this model uses the common expense, not a claimed reconciled cash deficit. No proven funding gap, current patient slots or gift price. Public/school-funded contracts are baseline, not donor-created delivery. Intern supervision, in-kind assistance and school infrastructure are not fully priced economic resources; a double-resource diagnostic is not a valuation.

evidence.design: Original FY2025 Form 990 and annual report
evidence.population: Whole legal recipient EIN 77-0393676, formerly Cleo Eulau Center
evidence.result: Both report $1,599,738 expense; IRS identifies $167,455 Beechwood counseling within broader spending.
evidence.transfer: Use whole expense; do not substitute program-only cost or infer funding room from deficit.

evidence.result: 484 sessions, including 31 family sessions; 19 average sessions/student. Satisfaction and coping observations, no controlled utility effect.
evidence.transfer: Count 24 index clients once. Completion is a judgment; family benefits and educator/SEL health are unquantified. Older hours and undated high-school page cannot silently replace current data.

evidence.design: Randomized CBT plus usual care versus usual care, economic analysis
evidence.result: 26.8 additional depression-free days and reported .067 QALYs at12 months. Simple .4×26.8/365 yields .02937; reconciliation unresolved.
evidence.transfer: No coefficient imported. Local younger/trauma-focused relationship-based care differs. Central conditional .06×.5×.5=.015 QALY per meaningful completed course is an analyst proxy before access adjustment.

evidence.result: Incremental .04 QALYs over12 months, CI .02–.09; substantial structured collaborative care.
evidence.transfer: Supports possibility of finite mental-health gains, not local effectiveness or mortality. ITT benefit is not divided by local completed sessions.

evidence.design: IMPACT randomized active-comparator adolescent depression trial
evidence.population: Adolescents with major depression assigned CBT, short-term psychoanalytic therapy or brief psychosocial intervention
evidence.result: No superiority of the specialized therapies over brief psychosocial intervention on the primary depression outcome.
evidence.transfer: Appropriate alternative care can sharply reduce added benefit; not evidence all therapy has zero effect. Supports explicit clinical-null and access uncertainty.

evidence.population: 680 educators and 874 SEL students in annual report; broader indirect reach
evidence.result: Consultations, coping/satisfaction and classroom skills are reported; no causal preference-based health effect.
evidence.transfer: Do not convert training or school reach directly to QALYs. Residual benefits are unknown, not zero.

reservations: Full-cost partial-health estimate is not complete organization value or directly comparable to complete multi-pathway models.
Twenty-four clients are reported; completion, utility, causal transfer and marginal cash response are judgments.
The favorable 10% world supplies nearly all signed expected health; removing it sharply worsens the price.
Annual report and older web descriptions differ in scope and throughput; current annual data take priority.
Existing program revenue and school/public resources may finance baseline capacity; no additional donor-ready offer is verified.
excludedBenefits: Educator support, SEL, training and school climate—unquantified, not zero.
Family spillovers without a deduplicated clinical denominator.
Suicide deaths averted inferred from crisis-intervention descriptions.
Academic achievement or subjective satisfaction counted as health utility.
